steps.tx: Screen for **Cushing syndrome** when the clinical suspicion is real, not for every obese patient. Two abnormal results among late-night salivary cortisol, 24-hour urinary free cortisol, and the 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test support the diagnosis. A morning cortisol of 1.8 mcg/dL or higher after 1 mg dexamethasone is abnormal. The drawing shows the stigmata that justify the screen, including moon face, a buffalo hump, purple striae, and easy bruising.

steps.tx: Once **Cushing syndrome** is confirmed, measure plasma **ACTH** before any scan. A value below 10 pg/mL supports an ACTH-independent adrenal source. A value above 20 pg/mL supports an ACTH-dependent source, either a pituitary adenoma or ectopic secretion. Values between those cutoffs are repeated. The left side of the drawing separates exogenous steroid, pituitary disease, ectopic ACTH, and an adrenal tumour.

vis.caption: The left panel draws four causes: exogenous steroid, pituitary Cushing disease, ectopic ACTH, and an adrenal tumour. The right panel draws the body habitus. No dexamethasone cutoff is printed (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Inferior petrosal** sinus sampling is the most accurate test to separate Cushing disease from ectopic ACTH secretion when the pituitary MRI is negative or equivocal. A central to peripheral ACTH ratio of at least 3 after CRH supports a pituitary source. A ratio below that does not, by itself, send the patient to adrenal surgery. Sampling is done only after biochemical Cushing syndrome is secure.

steps.tx: Do not **order** a **pituitary** MRI or an adrenal CT as the first test. Nonfunctioning incidentalomas are common, and imaging is interpreted only after biochemistry shows where the cortisol is coming from. A visible adenoma does not prove it secretes ACTH. Start with the screen, confirm the syndrome, then measure ACTH, and only then choose the scan.

steps.tx: **Alcohol excess**, severe depression, and poorly controlled diabetes can cause pseudo-Cushing physiology and an abnormal suppression test. The history is part of the test, and a single abnormal screen is not an operation. Pause and retest when the alcohol, the mood disorder, or the glucose is controlled. The body habitus on the drawing can be seen in simple obesity, so the biochemistry has to carry the diagnosis.

right.title: Pseudo-Cushing

steps.tx: **First-line** treatment of Cushing disease is transsphenoidal surgery. When surgery is not curative, options include repeat surgery, radiotherapy, or medical therapy. **Ketoconazole**, metyrapone, and osilodrostat block cortisol synthesis. Osilodrostat inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase. Medical therapy is a bridge or a fallback, and it is not a substitute for removing a resectable pituitary adenoma.

steps.tx: **Mifepristone blocks** the glucocorticoid receptor. Serum cortisol rises or stays high and cannot be used to judge control, so glucose and clinical features are followed instead. **Pasireotide** can treat Cushing disease but worsens hyperglycaemia, so it is a poor choice when diabetes is already severe. Neither drug replaces surgery when a pituitary adenoma can be removed.

steps.tx: **Nelson syndrome** is an enlarging corticotroph tumour with rising ACTH and skin pigmentation after bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing disease. The neck and the knuckles darken because ACTH is high and cortisol is absent. Subclinical autonomous cortisol secretion is a failed 1 mg dexamethasone test without overt Cushing stigmata, usually from an adrenal incidentaloma, and it is linked to hypertension, diabetes, and bone loss.
